resale_co.name: Resale Certificate of Occupancy (Certificate of Continued Occupancy)
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Mount Ephraim Construction / Zoning / Code Enforcement Office (Enforcement Officer is the Construction Code Official or designee)
resale_co.lead_time: Application and fee must be received before an inspection can be scheduled. Resale CO inspections are done on Tuesdays between 4:00 and 4:30 by appointment. Town code says the inspection is done within a reasonable time, not more than 20 days after a complete application.
requirements: Visible 911 house number, at least 4 inches tall, visible from the street
Sidewalks safe and free of hazards; no raised sidewalks or deteriorated concrete
Driveways and aprons: asphalt or macadam only for driveways; a deteriorated asphalt apron must be replaced with concrete
Handrails where there are three or more steps; steps 30 inches above grade need handrails on both sides; no more than 4 inch spacing between spindles
Porches with no perimeter railings must have railings installed (no more than 4 inch spindle spacing)
Peeling or chipping exterior paint scraped and repainted; unpainted exterior surfaces painted
Broken window panes repaired
Exterior electrical open splices or improperly installed fixtures corrected
Gutters and downspouts properly installed
Any hazardous condition the inspector finds must be corrected
Work done without permits may be cited and must be permitted and inspected
Open permits must be closed out (final inspections passed and certificate obtained)
Separate smoke alarm / CO alarm certificate from the Regional Fire Prevention Alliance before settlement

fees.label: Single family dwelling resale CO (2026 application)
Reinspection fee in town code, 1-2 family residences under 5,000 sq ft (Ord. 2024-15; differs from the $25 on the form)

resale_co.how_to_apply: Complete the borough's Application for Certificate of Single Family Dwelling RESALE and submit it with the $120 fee (cash or check payable to 'Borough of Mount Ephraim'). If mailing, address it to 'Attn: Construction', 121 S. Black Horse Pike, Mount Ephraim, NJ 08059. After the office receives the form and payment, call to schedule the inspection (Tuesdays 4:00 to 4:30 by appointment). Separately, schedule the smoke/CO inspection with the Regional Fire Prevention Alliance before settlement. The form also offers a 'Change of ownership ONLY' certificate with no inspection, but no one can occupy the property until the full CO is issued.

evidence.quote: Prior to the sale of any residential premises involving a new occupancy, the Enforcement Officer shall issue a certificate of continued occupancy in accordance with the standards set forth in Subsection A of this section.

The Enforcement Officer shall conduct an inspection of said residential building or portion thereof which is to be sold, within a reasonable time, not exceeding 20 days after completion of said application

In the event that any violations are found to exist, there shall be no new occupancy or use of the premises until the criteria has been satisfied for the issuance of the certificate of continued occupancy.
Fee for certificate of continued occupancy: $120.
Please Note: CO inspections are done on Tuesdays between 4:00-4:30 by appointment.
Application and fee must be received prior to scheduling any inspection.
Residential Home Resale Inspection Checklist-explanation and requirements.
APPLICANT MUST CONTACT THE REGIONAL FIRE ALLIANCE TO SCHEDULE A SMOKE DETECTOR, CO DETECTOR AND FIRE INSPECTION PRIOR TO SETTLEMENT.

resale_co.notes: The requirement is in town code Chapter 121, Certificate of Continued Occupancy (Ord. 14-08 of 11-6-2008), read in full through the ecode360 print view. Chapter 121 covers one-, two- and three-family homes, duplexes, townhouses and condominiums, but not rental units governed by Chapter 319 (Rental Property Registration). Fees are set in Chapter 127, section 127-2, as amended 12-4-2024 by Ord. No. 2024-15: $120 for a certificate of continued occupancy for one- and two-family residences under 5,000 square feet and under 30 feet tall ($174 for other buildings), and $30 for a temporary CO. The code lists a $50 reinspection fee while the February 2026 application says $25, so confirm which applies. The borough's current site (www.mountephraim-nj.com) sits behind a bot challenge and could not be read, so the February 2026 application and checklist were read from Internet Archive copies of the borough's own upload folder; both are scanned images, so quotes were transcribed from the page images. The 2026 application lists only a single family resale; no separate 2-family form was found. The 2026 checklist is an exterior list (plus permits); the older 2021 checklist also had interior, basement, plumbing, electrical and heating items. Office contact changed from tweiss@mountephraim-nj.com (2021 form) to tmartin@mountephraim-nj.com (2026 form); the 2026 form shows the main number 856-931-1546 without an extension. Rental registration (Ch. 319, Ord. 2024-11/2024-13) and Ord. 2025-01 (lead-based paint inspections, which by state law applies to rentals) are rental items, not resale requirements; they were not reviewed in detail.

requirements: Smoke alarms by construction date: pre-1975 homes need 10-year sealed battery alarms on each level including the basement; newer homes need AC powered interconnected alarms per the era table on the form
Smoke alarms on every level, outside sleeping areas, and at the bottom of basement stairwells
All smoke alarms must be less than 10 years old; someone must take them down and check the date on the back, and undated alarms must be replaced
Low voltage (alarm company) fire alarm systems must be tested by an alarm contractor before the inspection, with the certification shown to the inspector
CO alarm outside of but within 10 feet of all sleeping areas if the home has a fuel burning appliance, fireplace or garage; CO alarms must be less than 7 years old
House numbers: Arabic numerals at least 3 inches tall, contrasting, mounted at least 60 inches above ground and visible from the street

Secondary power source warning label (wording like 'CAUTION MULTIPLE SOURCES OF POWER', not handwritten) within 18 inches of the main electrical panel and meter if there is a generator, solar panels or battery storage
Everything must be done before the inspector arrives; an adult (18+) must be present at the start of the time block

authorities.name: Regional Fire Prevention Alliance (run by Barrington Borough)
authorities.area_served: Entire borough (the Alliance serves Barrington, Hi-Nella, Lawnside, Mt. Ephraim and Oaklyn)
authorities.lead_time: 14 or more business days before the change of occupant for the lowest fee; weekends, holidays and the settlement date do not count. Inspections are scheduled Monday to Friday, 9am to 2pm. Certificates are valid 6 months and are not transferable.

fees.label: Request received 14+ business days before change of occupant
fees.quote: 14+ business days prior to the change of occupant is $66.00.

fees.label: Request received 8-13 business days before
fees.quote: 8-13 business days prior to the change of occupant is $74.00.

fees.label: Request received 4-7 business days before
fees.quote: 4-7 business days prior to the change of occupant is $106.00.

fees.label: Request received 3 business days or less before
fees.quote: 3 business days or less notice prior to change of occupant is $171.00.

fees.label: Reinspection after a failed inspection
fees.quote: ALL FAILED INSPECTIONS WILL REQUIRED A $50.00 RE INSPECTION FEE.

fees.label: Penalty for change of ownership or occupancy without the certificate
fees.quote: the owner will be subject to a penalty of $500 per occurrence (N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.3).

authorities.how_to_apply: Fill out the Regional Fire Prevention Alliance smoke alarm certification application (fillable PDF) and email it to firealliance@barringtonboro.com, or print it and drop it in the mailbox at 205 Haines Avenue, Barrington, NJ 08007. Include a check or money order payable to 'Regional Fire Prevention Alliance'. Walk-in office hours are Tuesday to Friday, 8am to 2pm. Fees are non-refundable.

evidence.quote: The Regional Fire Prevention Alliance of Barrington, New Jersey serves the Municipalities of Barrington, Hi-Nella, Lawnside, Mt. Ephraim and Oaklyn.
Inspection is required per NJ Fire Code 5:70-2.3 for the selling, renting, or change of occupancy in one or two family homes.
CERTIFICATIONS ARE VALID FOR 6 MONTHS and are Non transferable. FEES ARE NON-REFUNDABLE.
A CHECK OR MONEY ORDER PAYABLE TO “REGIONAL FIRE PREVENTION ALLIANCE” MUST ACCOMPANY THIS APPLICATION.
TO CONTACT THE REGIONAL FIRE ALLIANCE, CALL 856-547-0991.

LEAID: 0425-001 Mount Ephraim Boro SMOKE DETECTOR COMPLIANCE Name: Regional Fire Prev Alliance Addr: 205 Haines Ave Barrington NJ 08007 Enf Auth. Municipal Fire Official Nicholas D'Alonzo Phone (856) 547-0991
Barrington Borough is the LEA for Hi Nella, Lawnside, Mt Ephraim and Oaklyn Boroughs.

fire_cert.notes: The Regional Fire Prevention Alliance is a shared fire prevention bureau run out of Barrington Borough under a shared service agreement; it is not a fire district. Its November 2025 application covers smoke alarms, CO alarms and the secondary power source label (CSACMASPSIL) and does not list a fire extinguisher requirement, which matches the 2025 state change (P.L.2025, c.19); an older December 2022 version required a 2-A:10-BC extinguisher. The form only mentions extinguishers in a reminder to check for recalled devices. Office: 205 Haines Avenue, Barrington. Fire code questions: Fire Official Nick D'Alonzo, fireofficial@barringtonboro.com; the NJ DCA fire directory lists him at ndalonzo@barringtonboro.com, (856) 547-0991. The borough also posted a copy of the Alliance form on its own site in February 2026 (Barrington-Smoke-Fillable.pdf).

other_items.label: Open permits and work done without permits
other_items.detail: Open permits must be closed out (remaining inspections passed and the certificate obtained), and work done without permits may be cited during the resale inspection.

other_items.label: Temporary certificate of occupancy fee
other_items.detail: Town code sets $30 for the first issuance and renewal of a temporary certificate of occupancy.

Fee and form for a 2-family resale (the 2026 application lists only single family).
Whether the current resale inspection is exterior only (the 2026 checklist is exterior) or still includes interior items.
Current direct link to the application on the borough's new website (the site could not be read; the archived copy of the borough's upload was used).
